descripcion: About FullStack FullStack is your AI-native engineering partner, built to turn AI capability into certainty. Most companies can demo AI; few can get it to production and prove what it produced. We close that gap with three capabilities, AI built into your products from the start, elite vetted talent who apply it, and transparent execution that shows value every step of the way. With now over 600 customers in North America, FullStack is one integrated partner for all your AI engineering needs. With FullStack, you move forward with confidence. We’re Most Proud Of Offering life-changing career opportunities to talented software professionals across the Americas. Building highly-skilled software development teams for hundreds of the world’s greatest companies. Having delivered hundreds of successful custom software solutions, which have positively impacted the lives and careers of millions of users. Our 4.1-star rating on GlassDoor. Our client Net Promoter Score of 68, twice the industry average. The Position Forward Deployed Engineers sit inside the client’s problem, not next to it. You embed with an enterprise team, help find the work that actually warrants AI, learn to architect the system, build it, and stay long enough to help make it survive contact with production. This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer. You will grow into pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering while learning to diagnose why retrieval quality collapsed after a data refresh. The people who succeed here are fast learners who join discovery conversations on Monday and help ship what was scoped on Thursday. On this track, your focus is data, retrieval, and model behavior : you help make agents trustworthy by getting the data, context, and evaluation right. We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up. How We Approach The Work FDEs are trusted to help shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for sound judgment, which you will develop over time: Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec. Decomposes the problem. Outcome → process → decisions → data → systems → actors → constraints — before choosing technology. Helps choose the intervention. Remove, simplify, traditional software, automation, LLM, RAG, agent, or multi-agent — and learns to defend why. Starts to recognize when the answer is a SQL query, not a vector database. Contributes to architecture decisions. Learns to document trade-offs (ADRs), set success metrics, and raise concerns about scope that won’t deliver value. What You'll Do Discover. Support workshops and process discovery with business, data, and engineering stakeholders. Help assess data readiness honestly. Learn to separate genuine AI problems from workflow problems wearing an AI costume. Structure the process and the spec. For any business process being automated, help map the current state, decision points, data inputs, and exceptions, then turn it into specifications that both people and AI systems can execute against reliably. Architect & design. Contribute to designing parts of agentic systems with emphasis on context and retrieval architecture — data sourcing, chunking, embeddings, vector and hybrid search, with exposure to reranking and permissions-aware retrieval — plus orchestration, MCP/tool integration, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Build. Help ship working systems — agents, retrieval services, evaluation tooling, and the data flows that feed them. Prototypes that prove value in weeks, not slideware. Engineer the delivery system. Contribute to CI/CD for what you build, extended to AI: prompt and context versioning, learning to add eval suites that run in the pipeline. Operate (Day 2). Support the team after launch — eval harnesses, groundedness and retrieval metrics, observability and tracing, cost and latency management, drift, and supporting the handoff that lets the client’s team run it without you. Consult. Help prepare and present decisions to CTOs, VPs of Engineering, CDOs, and business leadership. Learn to quantify impact in their terms. Observe pre-sales scoping and proposal work when the deal calls for it. What We're Looking For Engineering foundation About 1 year of hands-on experience across ML, data, and software engineering (flexible; internships, apprenticeships, and strong project work count) Python-first, clean-code mindset (typed, tested, deployed projects — not notebooks only); basic familiarity with TypeScript / Node, .NET / C#, or Java is a plus College graduate (bachelor’s degree) in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field Relevant certifications in AI/ML, data, or cloud (e.g., Azure AI Engineer, AWS Machine Learning, Google Professional ML Engineer, Databricks, or equivalent) Applied / operational AI Has built LLM or agent projects, ideally exposed to production environments (internships, open-source, or capstone work count) Working knowledge of retrieval and model behavior: embeddings, vector search, structured output, and prompting vs. retrieval trade-offs; eager to learn reranking, hybrid search, and model selection Hands-on with agentic tooling: Claude Code or similar AI coding tools, agent frameworks, MCP, and tool/function calling; curiosity about multi-agent orchestration Context and spec engineering: learns to design what the model sees — retrieval, context construction, specifications, process definitions, and memory — for reliable, context-efficient output Exposure to Day 2 topics: evaluation design (golden sets, LLM-as-judge, groundedness), observability, cost and token economics, failure-mode analysis Data and integration literacy: basic familiarity with ETL/ELT patterns, warehouses/lakehouses (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery), and integration options (APIs, event streams, iPaaS, MCP) — enough to understand them and contribute under guidance. Does not need to be an ETL/ELT specialist. Consulting & business Shows curiosity and early signs of the discovery behaviors above: business and personal drivers, constraints, stakeholder alignment, strategic questioning Interest in growing into client conversations (workshops, proposal walkthroughs, tough questions) as you gain experience Learning to translate technical decisions into business outcomes — accuracy, cycle time, cost per transaction, risk reduction, ROI Strong written and verbal communication in English; comfortable learning in front of senior stakeholders Strong Plus Additional certifications beyond the required ones (e.g., Databricks, Snowflake, or cloud data/AI specialty certifications) Public portfolio of work: GitHub projects, open-source contributions, or hackathon and capstone projects involving LLMs or agents Academic or project experience in classical ML (forecasting, classification, anomaly detection) alongside LLM work Internship or project experience with stakeholder-facing work, such as presenting demos or documenting solutions Comfort with ambiguity, fast learning, and switching between projects; prior internship or agency exposure is a bonus Nice To Have We’re Seeking Engineers Who Are AI-enthusiastic In Their Workflow. Professional Experience Or Personal Project Work With The Following Is a Significant Plus Cursor, Windsurf, or Google Antigravity. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, or Copilot CLI. FullStack will not sponsor applicants for work visas now or in the future. What We Offer Competitive pay in your local currency. 100% remote work. The ability to work with leading startups and Fortune 500 companies. English Classes. Ample opportunity for career advancement. Continuing education opportunities. descripcion: About FullStack FullStack is your AI-native engineering partner, built to turn AI capability into certainty. Most companies can demo AI; few can get it to production and prove what it produced. We close that gap with three capabilities, AI built into your products from the start, elite vetted talent who apply it, and transparent execution that shows value every step of the way. With now over 600 customers in North America, FullStack is one integrated partner for all your AI engineering needs. With FullStack, you move forward with confidence. We’re Most Proud Of Offering life-changing career opportunities to talented software professionals across the Americas. Building highly-skilled software development teams for hundreds of the world’s greatest companies. Having delivered hundreds of successful custom software solutions, which have positively impacted the lives and careers of millions of users. Our 4.1-star rating on GlassDoor. Our client Net Promoter Score of 68, twice the industry average. The Position Forward Deployed Engineers sit inside the client’s problem, not next to it. You embed with an enterprise team, find the work that actually warrants AI, architect the system, build it, and stay long enough to make it survive contact with production. This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer. You should be as comfortable pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering as you are diagnosing why retrieval quality collapsed after a data refresh. The people who succeed here can hold a discovery conversation on Monday and ship what they scoped on Thursday. On this track, your edge is data, retrieval, and model behavior: you make agents trustworthy by getting the data, context, and evaluation right. We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up. How We Approach The Work FDEs are trusted to shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for architect-level judgment: Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec. Decomposes the problem. Outcome → process → decisions → data → systems → actors → constraints — before choosing technology. Chooses the intervention. Remove, simplify, traditional software, automation, LLM, RAG, agent, or multi-agent — and defends why. Owns the architecture decision. Documents trade-offs (ADRs), sets success metrics, pushes back on scope that won’t deliver value. Consultative Discovery Clients rarely arrive with a fully formed problem, and the FDE’s first contribution is helping them see it clearly. You lead discovery with genuine curiosity, moving the conversation from stated requirements to underlying needs, and you build credibility through the depth of your understanding rather than the breadth of your pitch. Uncovers business drivers. What outcome matters, what it’s worth, why now, and what happens if nothing changes. Uncovers personal drivers. What each stakeholder is measured on, what they’re worried about, and what a win looks like for them individually. Surfaces constraints early. Security, compliance, data access, budget, skills, politics, timelines — the things that kill projects in month two. Aligns stakeholders. Spots conflicting goals between business, engineering, and risk, and brings them to a shared definition of success. Asks strategic questions. Follows the answer with “why,” “how do you know,” and “what happens today when…” — without interrogating. Clients leave the conversation understanding their own problem better. Earns authority through depth. Credibility comes from the quality of the questions and the insight in the playback, not from pitching technology. What You'll Do Discover. Run workshops and process discovery with business, data, and engineering stakeholders. Assess data readiness honestly. Separate genuine AI problems from workflow problems wearing an AI costume. Structure the process and the spec. For any business process being automated, map the current state, decision points, data inputs, and exceptions, then turn it into specifications that both people and AI systems can execute against reliably. Architect & design. Design agentic systems end to end with emphasis on context and retrieval architecture — data sourcing, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, permissions-aware retrieval, knowledge graphs where warranted — plus orchestration, MCP/tool integration, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Build. Ship working systems — agents, retrieval services, evaluation tooling, and the data flows that feed them. Prototypes that prove value in weeks, not slideware. Engineer the delivery system. Own CI/CD for what you build, extended to AI: prompt and context versioning, eval suites that run in the pipeline and gate releases. Operate (Day 2). Own what happens after launch — eval harnesses, groundedness and retrieval metrics, observability and tracing, cost and latency management, drift, and the handoff that lets the client’s team run it without you. Consult. Present to and defend decisions in front of CTOs, VPs of Engineering, CDOs, and business leadership. Quantify impact in their terms. Support pre-sales scoping and proposal work when the deal calls for it. What We're Looking For 5+ years of professional software development experience with core proficiency in Python (or TypeScript/Node.js). Has shipped at least one agentic AI solution, LLM workflow, or RAG architecture to a production environment. Intermediate English or higher is required. Advanced English is a plus. Bachelor's or technical degree in a related field (completed or in progress). Demonstrated hands-on experience using AI developer tools (such as Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or OpenAI Codex) in daily workflows. Track record of leading client-facing discovery calls to translate unstructured business requirements into technical architectures. Hands-on experience designing and integrating RESTful APIs, microservices, or event-driven architectures. Experience building agentic systems using orchestration frameworks or APIs such as LangGraph, LangChain, n8n, Model Context Protocol (MCP), or direct LLM APIs. Proven experience taking full end-to-end technical ownership of features from discovery to deployment. Ability to work through new and difficult issues and contribute to libraries as needed. Ability to create and maintain continuous integration and delivery of applications. Forensic attention to detail. A positive mindset and a can-do attitude. Experience working on Agile / Scrum teams. Meaningful experience working on large, complex systems. Ability to take extreme ownership over your work. Every day is a challenge to ensure you are performing to the expectations you and your team have agreed upon. Ability to identify with the goals of FullStack's clients, and dedicate yourself to delivering on the commitments you and your team make to them. Strong Plus Production AI operations (Day 2): eval harnesses, observability and tracing, cost and token economics, drift, debugging non-deterministic systems. Prompt- and eval-level regression testing running in CI and gating releases. Delivery in regulated environments (financial services, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing). Pre-sales support: discovery calls, SOW and estimate shaping, technical proposal defense. Process mining, operations analysis, or transformation consulting background. Client enablement and training — building the client team’s capability, not just the system. Prior consulting or agency environment; comfort with ambiguity and multiple accounts. descripcion: Accounting Manager Client Accounting & Advisory Services Location: Argentina Work Arrangement: Remote Employment Type: Full-Time About Convoy Finance We like working with people who move fast, think for themselves, and care about doing great work. That's pretty much how we run Convoy. We're a small finance and accounting firm working with technology, SaaS, fintech and Web3 companies across Canada and internationally. Our clients are ambitious businesses, and we work directly with the founders and finance teams building them. That means we're not just looking at numbers all day. We get to see what's happening inside growing companies and help the people running them make better decisions. One week you might be leading a month-end close, and the next you could be helping a client work through a reporting issue, improve their financial processes or solve something completely new. We're a small team, too. Most of us are based in Toronto, with a few people working remotely around the world. There's very little bureaucracy, decisions happen quickly, and good ideas can actually turn into action. The Opportunity We're looking for an Accounting Manager with a strong technical accounting background and experience gained at a leading international accounting firm. You'll oversee accounting work across a portfolio of growing companies and work directly with international clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You'll be responsible for making sure the accounting is accurate, the work gets done well and client deliverables stay on track. But we also expect you to look beyond the numbers: understand what's happening in the business, identify issues before they become problems and bring ideas to the table. This is a hands-on management role. You'll still be close to the accounting, while also reviewing work, guiding team members, managing priorities and helping clients navigate more complex accounting and finance questions. Our clients move quickly, and so do we. There will be deadlines, competing priorities and new problems to solve. As an Accounting Manager, you'll have significant ownership over your client relationships and the opportunity to grow into broader advisory, financial management and leadership responsibilities. What You'll Do You'll take ownership of: Managing a portfolio of client accounts, ensuring accurate and timely delivery of accounting and reporting work Leading and overseeing full-cycle accounting and month-end close, including reconciliations, journal entries, AP/AR and financial statement preparation Reviewing accounting work and ensuring quality, accuracy and consistency across client deliverables Preparing and reviewing financial statements, management reports and financial analysis Working directly with founders, CFOs and senior finance teams to answer questions, resolve issues and provide accounting guidance Managing client deadlines, priorities and deliverables, and proactively communicating when something needs attention Supporting year-end compilations, audits, reviews and tax-related work Identifying opportunities to improve accounting processes, systems and controls Coaching and supporting more junior members of the accounting team Taking ownership of more complex accounting issues and helping the team determine the right approach Supporting advisory and finance projects as they come up Building strong, long-term relationships with clients and becoming a trusted point of contact for their accounting needs Requirements What We're Looking For You have a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field and 5+ years of relevant accounting experience , including significant experience in full-cycle accounting, month-end close and financial reporting . Previous experience at a Big Four or other leading top 10 international accounting firm is required. We're looking for candidates who have developed strong technical accounting skills in a demanding public accounting, audit, assurance or advisory environment, with exposure to high standards of quality and complex accounting work. This is mandatory. You should have experience in public accounting, audit, assurance or client accounting and advisory services , with exposure to high standards of quality, complex accounting work and demanding client environments. You're confident owning full-cycle accounting, month-end close and financial reporting , while also reviewing work, managing priorities and ensuring that client deliverables are accurate and delivered on time. You're comfortable working directly with clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You communicate clearly in English and can explain what the numbers mean, not just what the numbers are. This role is 100% in English , both internally and with clients. You have experience reviewing or mentoring other accountants and are comfortable providing guidance, giving feedback and taking responsibility for the quality of the work delivered by your team. You're able to work in Eastern Time business hours. Availability from 9am to 6pm Eastern Time is mandatory. Experience with QuickBooks Online, Xero, Taxprep or CaseWare is a plus, as is experience working with SaaS, technology, fintech or Web3 companies . A CPA designation or active CPA pursuit is also a plus. Benefits Benefits Why Convoy? You'll work with interesting companies, smart people and problems that don't always come with an instruction manual. You'll have direct exposure to founders and senior finance leaders and get to see how growing companies actually operate. Because we're small, your work is visible and your ideas can have an impact. We're remote-friendly, with team members working from Toronto and different parts of the world. It's fast-paced. It's challenging. And it's definitely not boring. If you want a role where you can keep learning, take real ownership and grow beyond traditional accounting , we'd like to hear from you. Now, we’re building what comes next. HSS Data supports the enterprise side of HSS through four broad domains: Business, Clinical, Finance, and Research. The work is broader than machine learning. We build product features that forecast and predict various operational and clinical endpoints, test interventions, estimate program impact, find meaningful patient and operational segments, detect risk and anomalies, and build measurement frameworks when the question is not yet analytically well formed. We work in small “garages” with the people who own the problem, prototype quickly, and turn useful work into products and features that are deployed, monitored, and improved. The goal is velocity without sloppiness: get close to the work, build something real, measure whether it helped, and keep going. Job Summary We’re hiring Data Scientists at two levels to build advanced analytics and data-science-driven product features across HSS. Assignments will be fluid across the broad Business, Clinical, Finance, and Research domains based on organizational needs, the work underway, and a candidate’s strengths and interests. Data Scientist I. An early-career builder, generally with zero to two years of experience, who will usually begin with a narrower set of domains and problems. You’ll work with more experienced data scientists and domain experts to frame messy questions, build and test solutions, and personally learn to deploy, monitor, and improve models and features within applications and Databricks. Strong internship, graduate, or substantial applied-project experience can count. Data Scientist II. A more independent individual contributor, generally with three to five or more years of experience, who can own ambiguous work end to end and move across more than one domain when needed. You’ll find and shape opportunities, choose the right analytical approach, personally productionize and monitor the work, connect reusable methods across teams, and help earlier-career data scientists improve their game. What you’ll do Find and frame the right problems. Work with domain experts to identify opportunities, including needs that were never articulated as “data-science requests”. Turn vague questions — “what will demand look like next quarter?”, “why are cases running late?”, or “did this intervention actually help?” — into well-posed problems with explicit assumptions, a decision or workflow they will change, and a credible way to measure impact and value. Build data-science-driven products, not artifacts. Deliver advanced analytics and data-science-driven features through applications and real products (not stand-alone notebooks) that clinicians, operators, researchers, finance teams, and executives can rely on and keep using. Own or contribute across design, prototyping, development, testing, deployment, integration, monitoring, and iteration. Use the right analytical method for the decision. Apply predictive modeling and forecasting, experimentation and A/B testing, causal or program-effectiveness analysis, segmentation, anomaly detection, risk stratification, and novel measurement where each is appropriate. Challenge weak designs, quantify uncertainty, and know when a simpler method is the better answer. Personally productionize the work. Write maintainable code, integrate models and analytical logic into applications and Databricks workflows, create appropriate evaluation and monitoring, respond to drift or failure, and keep improving the product after launch. descripcion: A little about us: Culturally, it probably suffices to say that we take our work seriously, but not ourselves. Our leaders have spent time in the trenches and have cursed daylight savings time changes and trailing whitespace as many times as you have. We like to say that we spend 80% of our time cleaning the data...and 20% of our time complaining about cleaning the data. Joking aside, our voices matter, and it is easy to see how our decisions affect the Data Science practice and Red Alpha as a whole. We have a clear vision of where we are headed. Our team takes a pragmatic approach to Data Science, defining it loosely as the intersection of technical expertise, business acumen, and soft skills to solve business problems with data. We spend a lot of time trying to understand the problem before we set about building a solution, and we prefer lower tech useful solutions over shiny algorithms and dust on the shelf. Did we mention we’re pragmatic? We have a diverse set of skills across our team, and whether you are a traditional Data Scientist (whatever that means…), an Applied Research Mathematician, a Database Engineer, a Full Stack Developer, or something else in that neighborhood, if you have a knack for picking apart data to make sense of it, we would enjoy having a conversation with you. A day in the life: The Red Alpha Data Science practice grew out of Red Alpha's reputation in Software and System Engineering with our Department of Defense clients. As sometimes happens, customers who trust our expertise in adjacent areas asked Red Alpha to assist with some of their burgeoning Data Science problems. This role is hands-on across all areas as a data scientist; from understanding customer requirements and collecting data, to developing visualizations and advanced analytics to make data-driven recommendations and decisions. You will work directly with intel analysts to develop prototypes and novel solutions that satisfy complex operational needs. What you bring to the table: Now on to the fun of formal requirements - we have to apologize in advance for the corporate-speak here, but just hold your breath for a few lines and everything will be okay. We are actively hiring data professionals for roles across a broad range of skill levels and projects. Our goal is to find the best fit for you so please note that if you apply to one of them and we see a fit elsewhere we will let you know. So do not worry about applying initially for every position you might be interested in. All of our data scientists need the following skills: Proficiency with a scripting language such as R or Python Experience with data science techniques and algorithms such as classification, clustering, random forests, deterministic forests (jk), hierarchical modeling, deep learning, Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and others. Note that you do not need to have all of these (we hope you enjoyed our random smattering of techniques…!) but you should be comfortable and capable with several of them and know some others not on this list. A B.S. Degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Computer Science or related field. For entry-level data scientists, 0-3 years of experience on Data Science projects. For mid-level data scientists, 3-6 years of experience on Data Science projects. For senior-level data scientists, at least 6 years of experience on Data Science projects with at least 3 years of experience managing teams. A TS/SCI with Polygraph security clearance. For this particular role, you will also need: Large dataset experience Strong familiarity with data science applications such as association analysis, graph/network analytics, clustering, text analytics, classification and regression (multivariate and logistic). Training in the design and implementation of static and dynamic visualizations in R, Python, Tableau, or similar visualization software. These are important skills to have, but not necessarily mandatory: Exceptional interpersonal skills. descripcion: Summary This is an amazing opportunity to be engaged in the election process! The Department of Elections is searching for energetic and resourceful professionals who like to "get stuff done" . The Business and Finance Officer IV (BFO IV) position in the Elections Department combines an exciting, fast paced environment with the opportunity to cultivate talents and apply a variety of skills. About The Role : We are seeking an experienced, highly analytical financial leader to serve as a Business and Finance Officer IV (BFO). Reporting to the Administrative Services Manager, the BFO IV will provide expert guidance on financial strategy, budget development, resource allocation, and long-term financial planning. This position will develop and administer the department’s budget, ensure financial integrity and compliance, and implement financial systems that support data-driven decision-making. Our team is working to make our processes more agile, and this is an exciting time to join us. We are not looking for “business as usual”; we are looking for innovative individuals who want to help shape the future of financial stewardship and operational excellence within King County Elections. This role will interact with all levels of our department and operate with a high level of independence while collaborating with internal and external partners. This position is ideal for you if you enjoy solving complex financial challenges, collaborating with diverse stakeholders, and using data to support sound decision-making and accurate, secure, and accessible elections. Who We Are: King County Elections (KCE) manages voter registration and elections for more than 1.4 million voters in King County, one of the largest vote-by-mail counties in the United States. KCE's mission is to conduct accessible, secure, and accurate elections. As a leader in providing inclusive elections, KCE is focused on core values of accuracy, equity, integrity, service, teamwork, and transparency. The team at KCE is committed to ensuring all King County voters can get registered, cast their ballot, and make their voices heard. Learn more at www.kingcounty.gov/elections.aspx Who May Apply : This position is open to all qualified applicants. This position is open until filled. Applications submitted by December 21st will be part of the first round of review and interviews. Materials Required to Apply: Applicants must submit a King County Application, Resume, and Letter of Interest. The Letter of Interest should describe how your education and experience meet the qualifications and have prepared you to perform the essential functions of the job. Applications without the required materials may not be considered for this position. Job Duties Financial Planning and Budget Management Develop and manage biennial budgets, budget revisions, supplemental requests, and supporting financial documentation. Conduct complex financial analysis, forecasting, scenario planning, cost-benefit analyses, and fiscal impact assessments to support strategic and operational decision-making. Monitor financial performance, identify emerging issues, and develop recommendations to address budget variances and long-term financial challenges. Financial Systems, Reporting, and Analytics Design, develop, and maintain financial models, automated reporting tools, dashboards, and other analytical resources that support data-driven decision-making. Prepare and present recurring and ad hoc financial, operational, and project status reports for leadership and stakeholders. Drive improvements in financial reporting processes, transparency, and access to real-time financial information. Financial Compliance and Stewardship Ensure compliance with federal, state, county, and grant requirements, as well as internal controls, audit recommendations, and financial reporting standards. Develop financial reporting activities to ensure the accuracy, integrity, and reliability of financial information. Manage grant financial processes, including reimbursements, reporting, and documentation; ensure compliance with applicable standards, including Federal Uniform Guidance. Provide technical assistance on allowable grant activities, expenditure documentation, and internal controls for ensuring compliance. Manage the election cost allocation and jurisdiction billing process, including calculating election costs, issuing accurate and timely billing statements, ensuring compliance with RCW 29A.04.410 and other applicable requirements, and serving as the primary advisor to jurisdictional officials regarding election billing methodologies, costs, and payment obligations. Work closely with the department’s finance team to ensure accuracy in data and provide guidance on appropriate cost allocation. Strategic Advisory and Leadership Support Serve as a trusted financial advisor to department leadership by providing expert guidance on budget, financial, operational, and policy matters. Contribute financial expertise to support organizational priorities and long-term planning. Represent the department in countywide finance discussions and collaborate with internal and external stakeholders on financial initiatives. Process Improvement and Innovation Partner with leadership and cross-functional teams to evaluate business processes and identify opportunities for improvement. Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase efficiency, effectiveness, transparency, and service delivery. Foster innovation by implementing new tools, systems, and approaches that strengthen financial operations and organizational performance. Proactive Problem Solving Anticipate emerging financial, operational, and organizational risks, opportunities, and trends. Develop and implement strategies and solutions that support department and team goals and strengthen long-term organizational success. Experience, Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Four (4) or more years of progressively responsible experience in budgeting, financial analysis, accounting, or fiscal management, preferably in a large or complex organization. Experience developing, managing, monitoring, and forecasting complex budgets, including variance analysis and budget-to-actual reporting. Demonstrated ability to provide financial advice and recommendations to leadership and present complex financial information to diverse audiences. Demonstrated ability to anticipate challenges and opportunities and develop solutions that support organizational goals and informed decision-making. Strong knowledge of governmental accounting, budgeting principles, internal controls, fund accounting, and grant compliance. Advanced analytical skills, including financial modeling, forecasting, reporting, and data analysis. Experience using enterprise financial systems and reporting tools such as Oracle, PeopleSoft, Power BI, or similar applications. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft 365 applications. Strong project management, organizational, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, navigate complex issues, and deliver results. Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, and collaborative public service. Desired Qualifications Experience in public-sector budgeting, governmental finance, or election administration finance. Expertise in cost allocation, rate setting, grants management, or intergovernmental billing. Professional certification such as CPA, CGFM, or a related credential. Experience developing dashboards and reports using Power BI or similar business intelligence tools. Experience leading process improvement initiatives and implementing operational efficiencies. Competencies You Bring Financial Acumen: Interpret and apply an understanding of key financial indicators to make better business decisions. Manages Complexity: Making sense of complex, high-volume, and sometimes contradictory information to solve problems effectively. Strategic Mindset: Anticipating future possibilities and translating them into breakthrough strategies. Collaborates: Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives. Communicates Effectively: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. Action Oriented: Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm. The work site for this position is the Elections Building, 919 SW Grady Way in Renton. Work Schedule: This position is Exempt from the provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act and is not eligible for overtime pay. The workweek is typically 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. but may sometimes require work outside regular business hours during elections and other peak work periods. Travel to work locations throughout King County with limited or no public transportation services is required. A valid Washington State Driver's License is required to operate King County vehicles. Do you excel at driving efficiency and managing multi-location operations in a fast-paced, dynamic environment? As our Regional Operations Manager for Tea Around Town, you'll be the linchpin of our operational success across Texas, Georgia, and other assigned states. Reporting directly to the Director of Operations, you'll play a pivotal role in supporting our ambitious growth plans, leading cross-functional teams, and guaranteeing the seamless delivery of our unique mobile tea room experience. Drive Financial Performance: Analyze daily, weekly, and monthly reports to proactively manage labor, inventory, and cost controls, consistently achieving cost efficiency and exceeding product financial goals for each assigned location. Financial Stewardship: Collaborate closely with the finance team to develop and manage operational budgets, monitor expenditures, identify cost-saving opportunities, and uphold financial discipline. This role combines direct student service with data management responsibilities, ensuring accurate processing of financial aid awards and reliable reporting for institutional and regulatory purposes. This position is primarily office-based, with periodic evening or weekend hours during peak enrollment and financial aid processing periods (e.g., FAFSA season, orientation, registration). ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS: Financial Aid Coordination Counsel students and families on financial aid options, application procedures, and eligibility requirements. Review and process financial aid applications, including FAFSA data, verification documents, and appeals. Determine student eligibility for federal, state, and institutional aid programs. Analyze the relationship between aid packaging and enrollment yield to support merit and need-based aid strategy discussions with Admissions and Financial Aid leadership. Generate ad hoc and recurring reports for enrollment management, including net tuition revenue projections, discount rate analysis, and aid leveraging models. Support required federal and state reporting, including FISAP, IPEDS (including admissions and financial aid components), and state grant agency submissions. Compliance and Process Improvement Stay current on federal Title IV regulations, state aid program requirements, and institutional policy changes. Assist in preparing documentation for financial aid audits and program reviews. Recommend process improvements to increase efficiency and accuracy of aid processing and data reporting. Participate in training on regulatory updates and financial aid software systems. descripcion: Description Amazon's Global Logistics team is seeking a Senior Supply Chain Manager to own long-term capacity planning for the Global Cross-Dock (GXD) network. GXDs are origin facilities where freight from Selling Partners and Amazon's own procurement programs is received, consolidated, allocated, and shipped to 14+ destination marketplaces worldwide. In this role, you will be the single-threaded owner of capacity strategy across the end-to-end imports supply chain — from GXD origin nodes through ocean, dray, and destination processing — ensuring the right capacity is in the right place at the right time to support business growth. You will lead Amazon's long-range planning cycles (OP1/OP2/QxG) for GXD capacity, develop volume forecasts, partner with business teams on new marketplace and program launches, and govern capacity decisions through structured monthly and quarterly review mechanisms. This is a high-visibility role at the intersection of strategic planning and cross-functional execution, with direct impact on Amazon's ability to scale global imports efficiently. Key job responsibilities Own long-term capacity planning for the GXD network — including origin throughput, warehouse storage, and outbound container capacity — across Retail (DI/GPE) and FBA programs. Lead GXD inputs into OP1, OP2, and Quarterly Guidance (QxG) planning cycles by developing volume forecasts, capacity models, and scenario analyses that inform headcount, CapEx, and network design decisions. Build and maintain demand-to-capacity models that translate SCOT/S&OP topline forecasts into node-level capacity requirements across multiple constraint types. Partner with business teams (Direct Import, GPE, FBA Global Shipping) on new launch roadmaps, ensuring GXD readiness for marketplace expansions and program growth. Establish and lead capacity governance mechanisms — Monthly and Quarterly Capacity Reviews — providing end-to-end visibility from GXD origin through ocean, dray, and destination processing. Proactively identify capacity risks, develop mitigation strategies, and present data-driven recommendations to senior leadership. Collaborate cross-functionally with Ocean Procurement, Dray, Destination Ops, Finance, and SCOT to align capacity plans across the full imports supply chain. Drive continuous improvement by improving forecast accuracy, automating workflows, defining key capacity metrics, and building scalable reporting mechanisms. Our team operates in a fast-paced environment where data-driven decisions, cross-functional collaboration, and long-term strategic thinking are essential. Monitor production execution against plan, identify exceptions, quantify impact, and drive corrective actions. Build planning and scenario models to support cross-functional decision-making, leveraging AI and automation to reduce manual work. Position Summary The Senior Supply Chain Planner will play a critical role in advancing Banner’s inventory planning capability and stocking program strategy. This role will support and drive the processes, analytics, and cross-functional decision-making needed to improve in-stock levels at Banner and across distributor channels while balancing customer service, working capital, operational constraints, and product lifecycle priorities. The position will partner closely with Operations, Commercial, Product Management, Supply Chain, and regional teams to translate demand signals, stocking policies, service-level expectations, and product-family strategies into actionable inventory plans. The role will help define which products should be stocked, where inventory should be positioned, how stocking levels should be maintained, and how exceptions should be surfaced for decision-making. This position reports to Demand Planning Manager. This role requires working onsite at our Brooklyn Park, MN office five days a week. What You’ll Be Doing This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working Collaboratively and Individually, staying on top of tasks, and making a meaningful impact across teams and projects. Below are some key responsibilities of the role. Key Responsibilities Support the development and execution of Banner’s stocking program strategy, including P/S/N stocking recommendations, min/max logic, demand segmentation, and service-level targets. Analyze inventory availability, forecast inputs, demand behavior, backlog, open sales orders, lead times, and distributor requirements to identify gaps in in-stock performance. Partner with Product Management and Commercial teams to align stocking decisions with product-family strategy, lifecycle stage, customer promise, distributor expectations, and revenue priorities. Work with Operations and Supply Chain teams to translate stocking strategy into executable replenishment, production, and material plans. Develop reporting and dashboards to monitor in-stock levels, inventory health, service levels, forecast quality, slow-moving inventory, excess exposure, and stocking-policy effectiveness. Identify root causes of stockouts, inventory imbalances, past-due backlog, slow-moving inventory, and unmanaged stocking drift; recommend corrective actions and process improvements. Support monthly forecast and inventory reviews, product-family health reviews, and cross-functional stocking governance forums. Evaluate demand patterns using segmentation methods such as ABC/XYZ, runners/repeaters/strangers, lifecycle stage, customer concentration, and revenue contribution. Recommend stocking policy updates, safety stock assumptions, replenishment parameters, and exception-handling rules based on data, business priorities, and operational feasibility. Coordinate with distributor-facing and regional teams to understand channel inventory needs, availability gaps, lead-time expectations, and communication requirements. Help build standard work, planning tools, and repeatable processes that improve inventory decision quality and reduce reliance on ad hoc analysis. Escalate material stocking risks, service-level tradeoffs, or inventory exposure issues with clear options, financial impact, and recommended next steps. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to support individuals with disabilities. Required Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Finance, Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in demand planning, inventory planning, supply planning, operations analytics, commercial operations, or a related manufacturing environment. Strong analytical capability with experience translating large datasets into business insights, recommendations, and action plans. Experience with inventory management concepts including safety stock, min/max, service levels, forecast accuracy, lifecycle planning, SKU segmentation, and excess/obsolete inventory. Working knowledge of ERP, MRP, forecasting, planning, or inventory optimization systems; experience with Oracle, GAINS, Qlik, Power BI, Excel, or similar tools preferred. Ability to work cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Product Management, Sales, Finance, Customer Care, and regional teams. Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to both technical and business audiences. Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, structure problems, drive follow-up, and influence decisions without direct authority. Preferred Qualifications Experience in industrial manufacturing, automation, electronics, or distribution-supported business models. Familiarity with make-to-stock, configure-to-order, build-to-order, and engineer-to-order fulfillment models. Experience supporting SIOP, product lifecycle management, stocking strategy, distributor inventory programs, or product-family business reviews. Advanced Excel, data visualization, SQL, Power BI, Qlik, or similar analytics skills. APICS/ASCM CPIM, CSCP, or related supply chain certification preferred. Success Measures Improved in-stock levels for priority and stocked items at Banner and key distributor locations. Improved accuracy and discipline of stocking parameters, including P/S/N status, min/max levels, and replenishment assumptions. Better visibility to inventory gaps, stockout drivers, slow-moving inventory, and service-level tradeoffs. Clearer linkage between product-family strategy, commercial demand signals, and executable supply plans. Reduction in unmanaged inventory drift, excess exposure, and recurring planning exceptions. Repeatable reporting cadence and governance process for inventory and stocking decisions. Position Summary Lion Energy is seeking a detail-oriented, highly organized Purchasing & International Logistics Coordinator to manage day-to-day procurement and the international movement of products, components, samples, and equipment. This position owns the purchasing process from request and quotation through purchase order, approval, payment coordination, production follow-up, shipment, customs clearance, receipt, and record reconciliation. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across time zones with domestic and international suppliers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, warehouses, carriers, and internal teams. This person combines strong purchasing discipline with practical logistics judgment and maintains accurate, timely information in NetSuite and related tracking tools. Request and evaluate supplier quotations, including price, specifications, minimum order quantities, lead times, payment terms, capacity, delivery schedule, and estimated landed cost. Coordinate supplier selection and onboarding; collect W-9s, business and remittance information, product catalogs, pricing, minimum order quantities, lead times, and other required vendor documentation. Create, submit, revise, and close purchase orders in NetSuite, ensuring the correct vendor, SKU, quantity, price, accounting classification, ship-to location, and approval routing. Maintain visibility to pending and open purchase orders; follow up with approvers and suppliers, resolve workflow errors, and escalate delays that could affect production, sales, or customer commitments. Review pro forma invoices against approved purchase orders and resolve discrepancies before payment or shipment. Coordinate deposits, progress payments, final balances, wire confirmations, credit-card authorizations, and payment priorities with Finance and Accounts Payable. Track supplier production, sample, tooling, testing, and certification milestones and communicate changes in cost, scope, or schedule. Maintain productive supplier relationships and communicate clearly regarding orders, quality concerns, damaged or missing parts, corrective actions, and replacement needs. Inventory and Supply Planning Partner with Sales, Operations, Engineering, Program Management, and Inventory teams to align purchasing with demand forecasts, project schedules, safety stock, and available inventory. Monitor inventory and reorder points, support cycle or exception audits, and act early to prevent stockouts or excess purchases. Maintain accurate purchase-order, inbound-shipment, item-receipt, expected-delivery, and empty-return records in NetSuite and supporting trackers. Reconcile physical movement with system records; coordinate corrections to receipts, inbound shipments, quantities, dates, returns, and inventory adjustments when discrepancies are identified.
